title: What is it doing?
instruction: Read each mini-dialogue. What is the function of the bold expression? Choose a, b or c.

lines: A: Hi, Anna! How’s the new flat?
B: **Can’t complain.** The neighbours are quiet and the bakery’s just round the corner.
A: **Lovely day, isn’t it?**
B: Beautiful. I nearly asked them to hold the meeting in the garden.
options: starting a chat with a stranger

lines: A: Kat! You’ve vanished — we haven’t seen you at Friday lunch for weeks.
B: I know, sorry — **I’ve been really busy** with the Berlin launch. Next Friday, I promise.
options: explaining why you’ve been out of touch

lines: A: **It’s getting late**, and I’ve still got the dog to walk before bed.
B: Already? I’ll get your coat, Tom.
options: hinting that it’s time to leave

lines: A: So the samples will be with you by Tuesday.
B: Perfect. **Give my regards to** Mr Hughes — I haven’t seen him since the trade fair.
options: asking someone to pass on greetings

lines: A: That’s me done for the week, Pete. **Any plans for the weekend?**
B: Nothing big. My sister’s visiting, so a long walk and far too much cake.
A: That was the best pasta I’ve had all year, Sven.
B: **Let’s do this again soon.** Same place, but next time I’m ordering dessert.

title: Choose the right response
instruction: Complete each dialogue with an expression from the box. There are TWO extra expressions you don’t need.
bank: Are you here for the conference?

dialogues.title: Dialogue 1 — Hotel breakfast, before a conference
lines: A: Excuse me — {1} Every other table’s full.
B: No, go ahead. Plenty of room.
A: Thanks. {2} I saw the lanyards in reception.
B: I am — I’m speaking on Thursday, actually. Supply chains. I’m Sven, by the way.
A: Alita. I’m in logistics too, so I’ll definitely be there.
B: Great. Maybe we could talk afterwards — we’re looking for a partner in Poland.
A: I’d like that. {3} — the first session starts at nine and I haven’t even got my badge yet.
B: Here’s my card. I’ll call you on Monday, once we’re both back in the office.
A: Perfect. {4}

dialogues.title: Dialogue 2 — The queue at the local bakery
lines: A: Pete! I haven’t seen you since the summer. How’s everything?
B: Oh, {5} — work, football with the kids on Saturdays, and trying to keep the garden alive. And you?
A: Big changes, actually. I start a new job on Monday, and we’re moving flats the same week.
B: Both in one week? {6}
A: Thanks. Don’t worry — it’s only two streets away, so you won’t get rid of me that easily.
B: Right, that’s my bread. We’ve got friends coming for lunch.
A: {7} And enjoy the sunshine, Pete!

answers.2: Are you here for the conference?

title: Upgrade the reply
instruction: B’s reply works, but the opener in bold is the basic, safe choice. Replace only the bold part with a blue expression from the mind map that fits the situation better, and keep the rest of the sentence. The hint tells you what the situation needs.

lines: A: Anna? I don’t believe it! It must be two years since your leaving party!
B: **How are things?** Are you still at the bank, or did you finally open that café?
items.hint: it’s been ages — ask about the whole time since

lines: A: Morning, Pete! How’s the new office treating you?
B: **Not bad, thanks.** I was dreading the move, but I’ve got a window seat and the coffee’s free.
items.hint: things are better than you expected

lines: A: Morning! You must be here for the budget meeting.
B: **Hello, my name is Alita.** I’ve just moved over from the Warsaw office.
suggested: I don’t think we’ve met. I’m Alita.

lines: A: Hi, I’m Kat — I’ve just checked in. It’s my first time in Lisbon.
B: **Why are you here?** Work, or a bit of a holiday?
items.hint: ask politely why someone is visiting

lines: A: …and that’s the plan for the new website. Any other questions, Tom?
B: **Sorry, I have to run.** I know you’ve got a busy afternoon.
items.hint: leave, showing you respect their time
suggested: I won’t keep you any longer.

lines: A: Right, I think that’s everything. We’ll send you the full proposal on Friday, Ms Grant.
B: **It was nice talking to you.** We’ll be in touch once we’ve read it.
items.hint: formal — you’ve just met for the first time
suggested: It was a pleasure meeting you.

lines: A: Right, this is my floor. Welcome to the building, Tom!
B: **See you soon.** I’m sure we’ll bump into each other in the lift.
items.hint: casual — no plans, you’ll just run into each other

lines: A: Tom, we’ve been sitting here for three hours — they’re stacking the chairs!
B: **It was nice talking to you.** Same café next month?
items.hint: casual — an old friend you hadn’t seen for a while

title: Act it out
instruction: Work with a partner. Choose a situation and act out a short conversation from the first hello to the final goodbye. Use at least four expressions from the mind map, including at least two blue ones.
prompts: bumping into a former classmate by chance — in the street, in a shop or on the bus
waiting in a queue — making small talk with a stranger at the bank, the post office or a supermarket checkout
arriving at a family gathering — greeting relatives you haven’t seen for a while
running into a former colleague in a client’s building
welcoming a visitor from another office — walking them from reception to the meeting room
chatting to colleagues by the coffee machine on a Monday morning
finishing a meeting with a new client
